questions.q: Which of these is a common stage in quant recruiting, and what later lesson does it map to?
options: A math/probability screen, covered in Lesson 18
A mandatory coding bootcamp before any interview
A credit check as the first stage
An automatic rejection if you have other offers in motion
questions.explain: The math/probability screen is a common early-to-mid stage, and this chapter's Lesson 18 is built to prepare for exactly that round.

questions.q: How does the emphasis of a quant interview process typically differ between a systematic hedge fund and a prop trading firm?
options: There is no meaningful difference between the two
Systematic funds emphasize statistics, ML, and backtesting rigor; prop trading firms emphasize math/probability speed and real-time market intuition
Prop trading firms never ask technical questions at all
Systematic funds only hire through campus recruiting, never direct application
questions.explain: Systematic funds lean toward research methodology and statistics (closest to the SR-5 project); prop trading firms lean toward fast probability reasoning and market intuition.

questions.q: What is the recruiter screen actually evaluating, even though it isn't technical?
options: Nothing — it has no bearing on the outcome
Fit, logistics, and basic communication, including a prepared answer about your background and the capstone project
Your ability to solve brainteasers under time pressure
Your proficiency in C++ specifically
questions.explain: Though non-technical, the recruiter screen still filters candidates on fit, logistics, and how clearly you can describe your background and project — candidates can be screened out here.

questions.q: How long does a full quant recruiting process typically take, from first screen to offer?
options: 1-2 days
4-10 weeks
Exactly 24 hours, by industry standard
2-3 years
questions.explain: A full process commonly spans 4-10 weeks, and competitive candidates typically run several such processes in parallel.

questions.q: What distinguishes sell-side quant roles (bank quant desks) from buy-side roles (systematic funds) in typical emphasis?
options: Sell-side roles never involve any mathematics
Sell-side often emphasizes stochastic calculus and derivatives pricing; buy-side often emphasizes research methodology and live trading/strategy intuition
Buy-side roles are exclusively entry-level
There is no meaningful distinction between sell-side and buy-side quant work
questions.explain: Sell-side (bank) quant desks commonly emphasize derivatives pricing and stochastic calculus, while buy-side (fund) roles often emphasize research methodology closer to the SR-5 capstone itself.
